---
title: "minitrap"
---






`minitrap` provides two `purrr`-style function adverbs, `mtrap_safely()`
and `mtrap_quietly()`, that trap errors or console output instead of
letting them reach the console. See the
[README](https://github.com/djnavarro/minis/tree/main/minitrap) for the
full API reference and scope notes; this page walks through both in
action.

## `mtrap_safely()`

Wrap a function so a call that would normally error instead returns a
list with the error captured alongside a `NULL` result:




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
safe_log <- mtrap_safely(log)
safe_log(-1)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Warning in .f(...): NaNs produced
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
$result
[1] NaN

$error
NULL
```


:::
:::




A successful call returns the result with `error` set to `NULL`:




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
safe_log(10)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
$result
[1] 2.302585

$error
NULL
```


:::
:::




## `mtrap_quietly()`

Wrap a function so printed output, warnings, and messages are captured
instead of shown:




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
quiet_fn <- mtrap_quietly(function() {
  message("starting")
  warning("using a default")
  42
})
quiet_fn()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
$result
[1] 42

$output
[1] ""

$warnings
[1] "using a default"

$messages
[1] "starting\n"
```


:::
:::




`mtrap_quietly()` does not catch errors -- compose with
`mtrap_safely()` for that:




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
robust_fn <- mtrap_safely(mtrap_quietly(function() stop("boom")))
robust_fn()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
$result
NULL

$error
<simpleError in .f(...): boom>
```


:::
:::
